newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends higher on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends higher on short covering.

text.p: Renewed short covering in an oversold market boosted CME lumber futures late and prices ended higher, traders said.
Lumber closed mostly $3.40 to $5.20 per tbf higher with July up the least at $367.10 and September up most at $364.00 per tbf.
Midsession weakness on a continued weak undertone to cash markets lacked followthrough and September led the late rally to day's highs, traders said.
Cash sources said the market remained pressured from generally slack demand and excess production. Cash spruce may again be officially quoted lower overnight, they added.
